name: 46,XY Disorder of Gonadal Development

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Consensus Statement on Management of Disorders of Sex Development

criteria.description: Presence of 46,XY karyotype confirmed by cytogenetic analysis
Evidence of gonadal dysgenesis or streak gonads on histopathology or imaging
Presence of ambiguous or undervirilized external genitalia at birth
Abnormal sex steroid hormone levels consistent with gonadal dysfunction
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes associated with testicular development (e.g., SRY, NR5A1)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of 46,XY karyotype plus gonadal dysgenesis and ambiguous or undervirilized genitalia
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis may be supported by hormonal and genetic testing; clinical presentation can vary widely.

pathognomonic.notes: Includes micropenis, hypospadias, or bifid scrotum
searchTerms: ambiguous male genitalia with underdeveloped male features

pathognomonic.notes: Nonfunctional gonadal tissue confirmed by biopsy or imaging

searchTerms: high LH and FSH hormone levels

common.symptomName: Reduced or absent secondary sexual characteristics
common.notes: Includes sparse facial and body hair

occasional.notes: Breast tissue development due to hormonal imbalance
May be present in some cases

rare.notes: Malignant transformation risk in dysgenetic gonads

rare.symptomName: Psychiatric manifestations related to gender dysphoria
rare.notes: May occur due to discordance between genetic sex and phenotype
searchTerms: mental health issues from gender dysphoria
psychiatric symptoms related to gender identity
psychological distress due to gender incongruence

laboratory: Elevated luteinizing hormone (LH) and follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH)
imaging: Ultrasound or MRI showing streak gonads or absent testes
genetic: Pathogenic variants in SRY, NR5A1, DHH, or other sex-determining genes
other: Histopathology confirming gonadal dysgenesis or streak gonads

distinguishingFeatures: 46,XY karyotype with normal or elevated testosterone
Female external genitalia despite XY karyotype
Normal testosterone but low dihydrotestosterone levels

redFlags: Ambiguous genitalia at birth requiring urgent evaluation
Risk of gonadoblastoma in dysgenetic gonads
Delayed or absent puberty with hormonal abnormalities
references: Hughes IA, et al. Consensus statement on management of intersex disorders. Arch Dis Child. 2006.
Ono M, Harley VR. Disorders of sex development: new genes, new concepts. Nat Rev Endocrinol. 2013.
